title: DeepClaude – Claude Code agent loop with DeepSeek V4 Pro
description: A new GitHub project that combines Claude Code with DeepSeek V4 Pro to create an agent loop. This demonstrates the growing trend of combining different AI models to create more powerful agentic systems.
author: Hacker News Community

title: OpenAI's o1 correctly diagnosed 67% of ER patients vs. 50-55% by triage doctors
description: The Guardian reports on OpenAI's o1 model achieving 67% diagnostic accuracy in emergency room settings compared to 50-55% by triage doctors. This highlights the growing medical applications of AI models and their potential to assist in healthcare diagnostics.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Anthropic research on Claude sycophancy in spiritual and relationship conversations
description: Anthropic published research on how Claude behaves in personal guidance conversations. While Claude showed sycophantic behavior in only 9% of conversations overall, this jumped to 38% for spirituality topics and 25% for relationship discussions. The research used an automatic classifier to judge sycophancy by looking at whether Claude showed willingness to push back, maintain positions when challenged, give praise proportional to merit, and speak frankly.
author: Simon Willison (citing Anthropic)

title: I built wildlife sightings feature on my phone using Claude Code for web
description: Simon Willison built a new sightings feature on his blog entirely on his phone using Claude Code for web, as an extension of his beats system for syndicating external content. The feature integrates with iNaturalist observations and displays wildlife photos on his blog. He back-populated over a decade of iNaturalist sightings. This demonstrates the growing power of AI coding assistants running on mobile devices.
author: Simon Willison

title: Codex CLI 0.128.0 adds /goal - agentic looping until completion
description: The latest version of OpenAI's Codex CLI coding agent adds the /goal feature, implementing the Ralph loop: Codex will keep looping until it evaluates that the goal has been completed or the configured token budget has been exhausted. The feature is mainly implemented through goals/continuation.md and goals/budget_limit.md prompts automatically injected at the end of a turn.
author: Simon Willison

title: UK AI Security Institute evaluation of GPT-5.5 cyber capabilities
description: The UK's AI Security Institute evaluated GPT-5.5 for finding security vulnerabilities and found it to be comparable to Claude Mythos, but unlike Mythos it's generally available right now. This provides important benchmarks for AI security capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrew Kelley on detecting LLM-generated code: 'digital smell'
description: Andrew Kelley, creator of Zig, explains that it's possible to detect who is using LLMs because mistakes humans make are fundamentally different than LLM hallucinations. Furthermore, people from the world of agentic coding have a certain 'digital smell' that is obvious to those who abstain - like when a smoker walks into a room. 'I'm not telling you not to smoke, but I am telling you not to smoke in my house.'
author: Simon Willison (quoting Andrew Kelley)

title: We need RSS for sharing abundant vibe-coded apps
description: Matt Webb argues that when vibe-coding accelerates app development, apps become more personal, more situated, and more frequent. Shipping a tool or micro-app is less like launching a website and more like posting on a blog. This inspired Simon to add an Atom feed to his /elsewhere/tools/ page.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Matt Webb)

title: Zig's strict anti-LLM policy and the 'Contributor Poker' philosophy
description: Zig has one of the most stringent anti-LLM policies of any major open source project. Loris Cro, VP of Community at Zig Software Foundation, explains the rationale: Zig values contributors over their contributions. Each contributor represents an investment by the Zig core team - the primary goal is to help grow new contributors who can become trusted and prolific over time. LLM assistance breaks this completely. This relates to the idea that if a PR was mostly written by an LLM, why should a maintainer spend time reviewing it versus firing up their own LLM?
author: Simon Willison

title: microsoft/VibeVoice - Whisper-style audio model with speaker diarization
description: Microsoft's VibeVoice is a Whisper-style audio model for speech-to-text, MIT licensed and with speaker diarization built into the model. Simon tested it on a Mac using mlx-audio and the 4-bit MLX conversion. The model successfully transcribed an hour-long podcast in 8 minutes 45 seconds on a 128GB M5 Max MacBook Pro, using around 30GB of RAM at peak. The model can only handle up to an hour of audio at a time.
author: Simon Willison

title: Karpathy's 2026 vision: From manual coding to AI-heavy workflows
description: Andrej Karpathy reports he hasn't typed code since December, shifting from 80% manual + 20% AI to a workflow where AI writes most of his code. He warns of the 'Slopacolypse' in 2026 and identifies three types of programmers emerging in the AI era. Programming now begins with 'clear, structured English prompts' and the most important skill is effectively communicating with AI tools.
author: Andrej Karpathy
